_source: Our own table: the recipes of LuV's biofoundry, gtceu:biofoundry (docs/eras/luv.md, '4. Biofoundry', and decision 4, 'Living circuits at LuV'). Steps 1 to 8 are GTM's sterile chain, composed from GTM's live recipes (the plans below name them; the numbers are read from the loaded pack at every load): GTM's own recipes keep their sterile cleanroom condition, ours are the same steps under this type. Steps 9 and 10 are ours: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, the soil bacterium used as the vector that carries a gene into a plant (real practice, Zambryski et al. 1983; Hiei et al. 1994 for cereals such as barley; tobacco is the classic model plant for it). Steps 11 to 16 are UHV's xeno rows (docs/eras/uhv.md, package B4): Proxima b's genome data becomes a far-red gene cassette (the chlorophyll f genes, Ho et al. 2016) that transforms the ark's algae; four cultures serve Proxima's machines as kept catalysts: Cladosporium sphaerospermum (the radiotrophic vat), Chromobacterium violaceum (cyanide leaching of PGMs), Sphingomonas desiccabilis (BioRock's REE leaching) and Sporosarcina pasteurii (biocement).
_how_it_is_used: Read by server_scripts/grindless/luv/biofoundry.js at every server load (a /reload picks up changes). Each entry becomes one gtceu:sterile_culture recipe, id grindless:sterile_culture/<name> (GTM's builder puts the type in front). The smoke test gg_test_luv_biofoundry.js checks the live recipes against this table.

The programmed circuit is the step, one circuit per recipe: no recipe of the type may take a subset of another's ingredients (GTM's recipe lookup keeps one recipe per set of ingredients, counts ignored, and a recipe whose ingredients are a subset of another's can hide it).

composed[]: server_scripts/grindless/lib/compose.js reads `stages` from the loaded recipes, uses up `given` (the batch) and nets every `linked` key to zero (keys: 'i:<item>' or 'f:<fluid>'). The recipe takes and gives what the steps take and give, with the energy of every stage summed and spent at the highest EU/t of its stages (ceil(energy / that EU/t) ticks): GTM's own figures, never cheaper. GTM's sterile cleanroom condition is not copied: the hall is the cleanroom.
recipes[]: ours, at eut x duration. itemsIn / itemsOut: { id, count }; fluidsIn / fluidsOut: { id, amount } in mB.

Kept (the biofoundry refuses voiding): the diluted sulfuric acid goes back to sulfuric acid (GTM's distillery, distill_dilute_sulfuric_to_sulfuric_acid), the phosphorus back to phosphoric acid (GTM's phosphoric_acid_from_elements) for the next gelatin, and the stem cells' bacterial sludge back to mutagen (step 6).

Bacteria per NPU: about 1,000 mB of sterile medium per neuro processing unit (250 for the NPU, 250 for the organoid, 250 for the stem cells, 250 for its share of boards); that medium takes 1,000 mB of mutagen, which takes 10,000 mB of bacterial sludge: about 10,000 mB of bacteria, ten culture runs on Europa.

recipes._why: MAX-B4 (max.md, L12 step 1, c17): a pool of synthetic oligonucleotides, built on a phosphorus backbone from sterile medium and ammonia (Church 2012)
recipes.name: synthetic_oligo_pool

recipes._why: MAX-B4 (max.md, L28 step 1, c18): four oligo pools assembled on agar into the cassettes of a minimal genome (Gibson 2010; Hutchison 2016)
recipes.name: syn3_genome_cassettes
